analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Samsung slightly below; TSMC beats; CAP & DSY previews; Prosus estimates; Starlink licence approval; VOD UK raise
key_insights: Market overnight: QQQ fell 0.25% but recovered from morning lows. Semis and software declined while internet stocks gained. Analog, auto, semicap, neocloud and cybersecurity lagged, while memory, AI hardware, storage and beaten-up internet outperformed. GS describes the session as rotation and digestion, not a change in sentiment.

Firm memory pricing and supply constraints continue to support Micron and the memory outlook. A potential strike at Micron Taiwan is seen as positive for memory stocks because it could disrupt supply.

Samsung reported preliminary operating profit of KRW 107.4tn, slightly below the Street and a fourth consecutive record quarter. The shares slipped 1% as investors debated whether the result cleared a high bar. The desk sees it as good enough given the bar and attributes part of the miss to FX. The full divisional split comes 29 Oct.
Samsung is reportedly qualifying its 12-high HBM4E chips with Nvidia and hyperscalers (press report, not company-confirmed). AMD continues to explore a foundry partnership.
TSMC 3Q revenue reached a record NT$1.49tn (US$46.7bn), above the top end of guidance, driven by strong AI-chip demand.

ASML reports next week. The key question is whether there is room to surprise positively on the Q3 guide after the substantial Q2 guidance raise. Sell-side views are broadly bullish, buyside sentiment is mixed, and flows are two-way. US hedge funds appear to be using ASML as a sector funding short in favour of other semicap names, despite the stock looking inexpensive versus its own history and peers.

Terafab: Elon Musk said his companies will build and operate the chip plant independently, with TSMC potentially subleasing part of the facility. Intel is still expected to participate, including through a reported collaboration with UMC on 12-inch fabrication. Intel's 14A process remains part of the project.

Capgemini Q3 preview: GIR raises organic growth forecasts to 3.8% for Q3 and 3.2% for Q4, implying 4.1% for FY26, slightly above guidance. FY27 consensus growth of 3.2% looks well supported by potential WNS synergies. Agentic AI creates longer-term uncertainty for IT services, but Capgemini's position and restructuring should support margins.

Dassault Systemes (DSY) preview: GS says the core Industrial Innovation business is healthy but wants clearer evidence of a sustained recovery in Life Sciences, ARR and AI monetisation before turning more constructive. GIR models FY26 revenue growth at the guidance midpoint (c.4% y/y ex-FX) and sees the low end of guidance as largely de-risked. The stock trades near 15-year trough multiples and investor sentiment is bearish. Neutral, EUR 21 target. CMD in November.

Prosus CEO letter: JET returned to order growth after 55 months of decline and iFood is holding share in Brazil. GS reads FY27 adj. EBITDA guidance for iFood and JET as at the lower end of prior ranges. iFood consensus EBITDA is $134mn versus guidance of $100-150mn. JET consensus is $95mn versus guidance of $100mn+. Tencent remains the bigger driver.

Vodafone upgraded mid-to-long-term synergy and EBITDA/OpFCF guidance for its UK business: mid-to-high-single-digit EBITDA CAGR over FY25-32 and OpFCF tripling over the period. GIR expects consensus OpFCF to rise 1-2% by FY29/30. The upgrade was expected ahead of the UK investor day.

The FCC authorised SpaceX to launch 15,000 next-generation low-orbit satellites for Starlink Mobile and sell direct-to-phone service without relying on a terrestrial carrier's spectrum agreement. It would use EchoStar and T-Mobile frequencies, targeting up to 150 Mbps on standard phones. This adds competition for telecom operators.

Broadcom is exploring about $30bn of debt financing to help OpenAI buy custom AI chips, after a $60bn financing for Anthropic's AI infrastructure. Oracle and SpaceX are also seeking similar financing.

Adyen: the EGM approved board changes. Chris Vogelzang joins the Supervisory Board, Piero Overmars retires 1 Nov, and Herna Verhagen becomes chair. An executive leadership model change takes effect 31 Jan 2027. The desk says it makes little difference. Q3 update is 28 Oct and GS estimates are largely unchanged.

LG Electronics' 3Q miss points to weaker appliance and vehicle-component margins and implies LG Innotek operating profit of about KRW 80bn versus expectations of KRW 90-130bn. Rising memory prices push OEMs to seek savings in non-memory components, adding downside risk for camera modules and display-panel pricing.
Samsung's MX division is said to cut 4Q26 smartphone production by up to 30% as memory prices hurt profitability. Samsung has not decided supply size or mass production schedules for HBM4E.
Taiwan banned imports of Chinese-made fiberglass silicone sleeves, triggering a speculative surge in Taiwanese fiberglass stocks. Nanya (1303) and Taiwan Glass (1802) hit limit up.

Micron Taiwan's Taoyuan union reported 88.3% of members voted to strike. The Taichung plant and union hold second-round talks 10/22 and may also vote to strike. Local press says this may affect memory supply.

UK telecoms: VMO2's CEO urged DCMS not to fast-track BT's GBP 400m acquisition of TalkTalk Consumer and PlatformX. The CMA could report as early as 19 October. BDO warned of a material going-concern uncertainty at CityFibre, citing limited covenant headroom by June 2027. CityFibre plans a GBP 900m shareholder raise.
Telefonica: Spain restarted the award of the EUR 100mn-plus CORA III cybersecurity and data-centre interconnection contract, ending a 14-month legal dispute.

Informa analyst trip: the analyst is more bullish. Management sees the pharma events franchise led by CPHI positioned for sustained growth, with under-monetised opportunities in attendee monetisation, lead generation, matchmaking and digital products.
BBC and Channel 4 are in preliminary talks on a commercial JV per Reuters. One option folds C4's ad operations, E4/Film4 and VOD into BBC Studios' UKTV, leaving the flagship channel outside.

Online Travel Q3 preview: GS industry work points to a broadly stable to strong demand environment, most pronounced in the US in the September quarter. Investor focus: forward commentary on unit pricing, agentic AI opportunities versus challenges, and growth investment versus 2027 operating margins.

Positioning: clients re-engaged in Tech, taking Mag 7 net exposure to near 22% of total US exposure, the highest since 2022. Semis and Semi Equipment are about 12% versus about 6% at the start of the year. US Tech was the only sector net bought on the Prime book in September, with the largest monthly buying since Feb 2025. Overall net positioning is still low, with US Fundamental L/S nets in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback.
